vectors.name: saturn-kronos-keeps-the-same-backup-ram-elsewhere
vectors.rationale: Beetle Saturn's .bkr and Kronos's kronos/saturn/<stem>.ram are the same 32 KiB of backup RAM; Kronos's backup cartridge depends on an option its save answer does not read, so whether it keeps one is unestablished and the answer says why. Beetle's .smpc is the console's own clock and settings, no part of the game's save, and the record sets it aside with its citation (#577 D13).

vectors.name: saturn-kronos-with-beetle-saves-reads-beetles-files-in-place
vectors.rationale: With kronos_use_beetle_saves enabled Kronos opens <stem>.bkr and puts a 4 Mbit backup cartridge in at <stem>.bcr in the save directory, the files Beetle Saturn wrote, in the same layout: both read in place, and the save carries over whole — the .smpc beside them is the console's, not the game's (#577 D13).

vectors.name: saturn-kronos-with-beetle-saves-leaves-the-declared-cartridge-unestablished
vectors.rationale: Before either core has written a save, Kronos's declared answer with kronos_use_beetle_saves enabled names <stem>.bkr and keeps <stem>.bcr an observation candidate: the switch names the 4 Mbit cartridge, but the emulator's game table replaces the cartridge for the discs it lists (DBLookup, ctrl/src/yabause.c:392-393 at 6709c1d), and atlas reads no disc. The backup RAM is the same file; whether Kronos keeps a cartridge for this game is unestablished, and the caveat says why.

vectors.name: a-system-no-format-record-covers-states-why-it-is-unestablished
vectors.rationale: No packaged save-format record covers either Game Boy Advance core yet, so both sides say so and the pair is unestablished rather than guessed from the file names.

vectors.name: gb-mesen-s-to-sameboy-states-its-mbc3-ram-apart
vectors.rationale: Mesen-S keeps plain, MBC1, MBC2 and MBC5 cartridges' RAM as the same raw image SameBoy keeps. For an MBC3 cartridge, with a clock or not, it maps RAM bank n at byte offset n rather than at n × 0x2000 (Core/GbMbc3.h:36 at 9e4fdeb): the first bank lies where SameBoy reads it, every further one overlaps, and whether a save uses them is the header's, which atlas does not read, so MBC3 is unestablished (#577 D17). Its MBC5 bank select keeps a rumble cartridge's motor bit, so that kind is unestablished too. Mesen-S writes no clock, so there is no clock part; the RAM answers unestablished with each kind stated.

vectors.name: gb-gambatte-to-sameboy-states-the-ram-and-the-clock-per-cartridge-kind
vectors.rationale: Gambatte and SameBoy keep a Game Boy cartridge's RAM as the same raw image in <stem>.srm for MBC1, MBC2, MBC3 and MBC5 cartridges. Gambatte writes its .rtc, a base time SameBoy does not keep, only for an MBC3 or HuC3 cartridge with a clock: for those the clock does not carry over, and for every other kind there is no clock and nothing to lose (#577 D16). Where no read establishes a kind's layout on either side (a cartridge with RAM and no mapper on Gambatte, HuC1 and HuC3 on most cores, an MBC5 cartridge with rumble where the motor bit can select a bank, MBC2 between cores that keep a write through a mirror differently), that kind is unestablished rather than folded into the others (#577 D15). Both parts answer unestablished and state each kind.

vectors.name: gb-sameboy-to-gambatte-states-the-clock-per-cartridge-kind
vectors.rationale: SameBoy writes its clock section for every cartridge with a battery, a clock or not (#577 D10), and Gambatte reads none of it: for an MBC3 or TPP1 cartridge's clock that is the clock lost, for every other kind the file holds no game data and nothing is lost (#577 D16). The RAM carries over in place for the kinds both read alike, and not for the MMM01, MBC7, TPP1 and Pocket Camera cartridges SameBoy runs and Gambatte refuses. Where no read establishes a kind's layout on either side (a cartridge with RAM and no mapper on Gambatte, HuC1 and HuC3 on most cores, an MBC5 cartridge with rumble where the motor bit can select a bank, MBC2 between cores that keep a write through a mirror differently), that kind is unestablished rather than folded into the others (#577 D15).

vectors.name: gb-gambatte-to-mgba-states-the-mbc2-ram-apart
vectors.rationale: mGBA packs an MBC2 cartridge's 512 four-bit cells two to a byte, where Gambatte keeps one to a byte, so for that kind RetroArch hands mGBA a layout it reads as its own and the RAM does not carry over; for the plain bank kinds it carries over in place. The clock, a base time mGBA does not keep, is lost for a clock cartridge and holds nothing for the others. Where no read establishes a kind's layout on either side (a cartridge with RAM and no mapper on Gambatte, HuC1 and HuC3 on most cores, an MBC5 cartridge with rumble where the motor bit can select a bank, MBC2 between cores that keep a write through a mirror differently), that kind is unestablished rather than folded into the others (#577 D15).

vectors.name: gb-gearboy-to-vba-m-states-the-pocket-camera-ram-apart
vectors.rationale: Gearboy and VBA-M keep the same raw cartridge RAM for MBC1, MBC2 and MBC5 and the same 48-byte MBC3 clock. Gearboy's MBC3 bank select stops at bank 3 where an MBC30 goes to 7, so its MBC3 RAM is unestablished (#577 D17), and it runs the Pocket Camera as an MBC3 and keeps only its first four RAM banks, where VBA-M keeps none of the camera's RAM in its save: for that kind the RAM does not carry over. The clock carries over in place where a cartridge has one; VBA-M's HuC3 and TAMA5 clocks are no question here, because Gearboy runs neither cartridge. Where no read establishes a kind's layout on either side (a cartridge with RAM and no mapper on Gambatte, HuC1 and HuC3 on most cores, an MBC5 cartridge with rumble where the motor bit can select a bank, MBC2 between cores that keep a write through a mirror differently), that kind is unestablished rather than folded into the others (#577 D15).

vectors.name: gb-gambatte-to-vba-m-states-the-mbc2-mirror-apart
vectors.rationale: Gambatte and VBA-M keep an MBC2 cartridge's 512 cells one to a byte, but Gambatte keeps a write through a mirror of them at its window offset, past the cells, while VBA-M drops it (#577 D18): a game that writes through a mirror leaves a save VBA-M does not hold whole, so for MBC2 the RAM is unestablished. Gambatte's clock, a base time VBA-M does not keep, does not carry over for a clock cartridge and holds nothing for the rest. The kinds no read establishes on either side stay unestablished as well (#577 D17).

vectors.name: gb-vba-m-to-mgba-states-the-clock-per-cartridge-kind
vectors.rationale: VBA-M writes a clock for MBC3, HuC3 and TAMA5 cartridges. mGBA reads the MBC3 one as it lies and keeps no clock for HuC3 and TAMA5 although it runs both. For the RAM, mGBA packs MBC2 its own way, and VBA-M keeps no TAMA5 or Pocket Camera memory in its save, so those kinds hold no game data. Where no read establishes a kind's layout on either side (a cartridge with RAM and no mapper on Gambatte, HuC1 and HuC3 on most cores, an MBC5 cartridge with rumble where the motor bit can select a bank, MBC2 between cores that keep a write through a mirror differently), that kind is unestablished rather than folded into the others (#577 D15).

vectors.name: gb-tgb-dual-to-doublecherrygb-states-the-hudson-kinds-apart
vectors.rationale: DoubleCherryGB is a TGB Dual fork with the same cartridge RAM and the same 4-byte clock written for every game, so for the plain bank kinds the save carries over in place, and where a cartridge has no clock the file holds nothing to lose. Neither core's HuC1, HuC3 or MMM01 banking is read (MMM01 runs for one title the code names), so those kinds are unestablished (#577 D15), and TAMA5 memory, which neither keeps, holds no game data.

vectors.name: gb-sameboy-to-mesen-s-states-the-ram-and-the-clock-per-cartridge-kind
vectors.rationale: Mesen-S runs plain, MBC1, MBC2, MBC3 and MBC5 cartridges and keeps no cartridge clock at all. SameBoy's RAM carries over in place for the plain, MBC1, MBC2 and MBC5 ones; MBC3, whose banks past the first Mesen-S overlaps, is unestablished, and the others SameBoy runs do not carry over; its clock section, written for every battery cartridge, is a clock lost for a cartridge with one and nothing lost for the rest (#577 D16). Both parts answer unestablished with each kind's verdict, the clock with no target group.

vectors.name: gbc-reads-the-game-boy-records
vectors.rationale: A Game Boy Color cartridge's save is laid out as a Game Boy one's, so each record states gbc as the same as gb: the pair answers exactly as on gb.

vectors.name: gb-bsnes-has-no-record-for-a-game-boy-cartridge
vectors.rationale: bsnes runs a Game Boy cartridge through its Super Game Boy and writes the save itself; no packaged record states what that file holds, so the pair says so and is unestablished.

vectors.name: nds-desmume-2015-to-desmume-moves-the-dsv
vectors.rationale: Both DeSmuME builds keep a DS card's save in <stem>.dsv: the raw save memory, padded with 0xFF as far as the game wrote, and the same 122-byte footer, which each reads back at the size the footer states. The .dsv moves from DeSmuME 2015's working directory to the save directory; the .dsv.bak DeSmuME 2015's card lists is a copy this build never writes or reads, so it is set aside with its citation.

vectors.name: nds-melonds-to-melonds-ds-sizes-the-save-per-game-apart
vectors.rationale: melonDS 0.9.3 and melonDS DS keep the same raw save memory, but each sizes it by the save type its own ROM list gives the game's code, and the two lists differ for some codes, so a game's save may be cut or padded on the way. atlas reads no game code, so the part is unestablished and names each side's list (#577 D19).

vectors.name: nds-desmume-to-melonds-standalone-sizes-the-save-per-game-apart
vectors.rationale: DeSmuME's .dsv is as long as the game wrote, padded to its own table and followed by a footer; melonDS 1.1 sizes the save by its ROM list and reads a file up to that length. Whether a game's save survives depends on how the two lengths meet for that game, which atlas cannot tell without the game code, so the part is unestablished for that reason rather than for the footer, which the research records (#577 D19).

vectors.name: nds-melonds-to-desmume-does-not-count-desmume-s-own-import
vectors.rationale: DeSmuME imports a raw <stem>.sav only while no .dsv exists and only at a size its own table names, which has no 128 KiB chip; that import is the target's own and not counted as reading melonDS's format, so the part is unestablished with each side's length named (#577 D19).

vectors.name: nds-noods-has-no-record
vectors.rationale: NooDS keeps its own <stem>.sav, and no packaged record states what that file holds, so the pair says so and is unestablished.

vectors.name: gc-dolphin-to-dolphin-core-moves-each-region-s-gci-folder
vectors.rationale: Dolphin and its core keep slot A as a GCI folder by default, one per region, each save a .gci of its directory entry and its blocks, read and written alike in both builds. A game runs in one region on both sides, so each region's folder is a part of its own (#577 D21) and carries over to the core's folder of the same region below its User tree.

vectors.name: gc-dolphin-raw-card-to-primehack-gci-folder-is-convertible
vectors.rationale: With a raw card in slot A and a GCI folder in slot B, Dolphin's slot A card converts to PrimeHack's slot A folder of the same region through Dolphin's memory-card manager, which exports a card's saves as .gci files, with no rule a client applies itself; PrimeHack keeps nothing in slot B, so the slot B folders do not carry over (#577 D8).

vectors.name: gc-primehack-gci-folder-to-dolphin-raw-card-is-convertible
vectors.rationale: PrimeHack's GCI folder converts to Dolphin's raw card of the same region through the memory-card manager, which imports each .gci into the card and re-signs the copy-protected saves to it.

vectors.name: gc-swapped-raw-card-paths-label-each-card-by-its-slot
vectors.rationale: Dolphin.ini points slot A at a file named MemoryCardB and slot B at one named MemoryCardA. A configured card path names the slot's card whatever the file is called, the running disc's region in place of the name's region word, so each card is the part of the slot that reads it, not of the slot its name suggests, and carries over to PrimeHack's card of the same slot and region.

vectors.name: gc-content-with-no-region-leaves-each-card-unestablished
vectors.rationale: A .dol names no region in its header: Dolphin boots it as an executable whose region is Unknown and runs it in [Core] FallbackRegion, by default the system locale's, which atlas does not read and two emulators may hold differently, so each region's card part is unestablished (#577 D22).

vectors.name: gc-a-renamed-card-in-slot-a-is-slot-a-s-beside-a-default-slot-b
vectors.rationale: Dolphin.ini points slot A at a file called MemoryCardB in a folder of its own and leaves slot B at its default card. Each card is the part of the slot whose path names it, so slot A's card carries over to PrimeHack's slot A card of the same region, and slot B's does not carry over to PrimeHack, which keeps nothing in slot B.

vectors.name: gc-two-cards-of-one-name-are-each-the-slot-whose-folder-names-it
vectors.rationale: Dolphin.ini gives both slots a card called Mine.raw in two folders. A card is the slot's whose path names its folder as well as its name, so each region has one slot A and one slot B part.

vectors.name: gc-a-gba-cartridge-adapter-has-no-record
vectors.rationale: A GBA cartridge adapter in slot A keeps the cartridge's save beside the cartridge, and no packaged record states what that file holds, so the pair says so and is unestablished.

vectors.name: gc-a-configured-gci-folder-has-no-record
vectors.rationale: A GCI folder Dolphin.ini moves elsewhere is a directory no rule names: every GCI folder rule names the `<region>/Card <slot>` folder below the card tree, so the pair says save-format-unrecorded and is unestablished rather than reading a verdict off a folder no record states.

vectors.name: wii-dolphin-to-primehack-moves-the-title-data
vectors.rationale: A Wii title's save is the files of its data directory in each emulator's NAND, one host file per NAND file, in every build alike; a file the NAND's own metadata does not list is given read and write for everyone, so the directory carries over to PrimeHack's NAND as it lies. Dolphin's NAND sits where RetroDECK's Dolphin.ini puts it.

vectors.name: wii-dolphin-core-to-dolphin-moves-the-title-data
vectors.rationale: The Dolphin core keeps the NAND below its User tree in the save directory, and its title data carries over to Dolphin's NAND the same way.

vectors.name: gc-two-cards-in-folders-of-one-name-are-each-their-own-slots
vectors.rationale: Dolphin.ini gives each slot a card called Mine.raw in two folders that end alike, /x/GC and /y/GC. The save answer states which slot reads each card, so each is its own slot's part, whatever the folders share (#577 D23).

vectors.name: gc-a-card-named-like-the-other-slots-default-in-a-folder-ending-in-gc
vectors.rationale: Dolphin.ini points slot A at a file called MemoryCardB in a folder that happens to end in GC, as Dolphin's own card folder does, and leaves slot B at its default card. Each card is the part of the slot that reads it, so slot A's carries over to PrimeHack's slot A and slot B's does not carry over to PrimeHack, which keeps nothing in slot B (#577 D23).

vectors.name: gc-a-sandbox-path-and-a-host-path-of-one-name-are-each-their-own-slots
vectors.rationale: Slot A's card path is inside Dolphin's sandbox and slot B's on the host, both ending in dolphin-emu/GC/Mine.raw. The save answer resolves each slot's path, sandbox included, so each card is its own slot's part (#577 D23).

vectors.name: gc-both-slots-on-one-card-are-a-part-of-each
vectors.rationale: Dolphin.ini sets both slots to one card. The save answer states the file once, read by both slots, and the pair makes a part of it for each slot, each carrying over to PrimeHack's card of that slot and region (#577 D23).

vectors.name: gc-slot-a-on-slot-b-s-default-card-reads-it-for-both
vectors.rationale: Dolphin.ini points slot A at MemoryCardB in Dolphin's own card folder, the file slot B opens by default, so one card is read by both slots: toward PrimeHack, which keeps nothing in slot B, slot A's part carries over and slot B's does not (#577 D23).

vectors.name: psx-duckstation-s-first-card-named-like-the-second-s-default-is-the-first-card
vectors.rationale: DuckStation's settings name slot 1's shared card shared_card_2.mcd in a folder of its own. The save answer states that slot 1 reads it, so it is the first card's part and carries over to SwanStation's first card, whatever its name spells (#577 D23).

vectors.name: gc-a-configured-card-named-with-jpn-keeps-it
vectors.rationale: Dolphin 2609 cuts USA, JAP, EUR and DEV from the end of a configured card's name before it puts the running disc's region there, and not JPN, so a card configured as Mine.JPN.raw is opened as Mine.JPN.USA.raw and so on per region; the save answer names those files, and they carry over to PrimeHack's slot A card of each region.
